To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pinning potential barriers in HTc superconducting multilayer systems are strongly affected by the transport currents, and the critical current density of these superconductors can be significantly increased by irradiation.

the pinning of vortices in multilayer HTc superconducting materials can be described as a process of interaction between pancake vortices and nano-sized defects, which is a consequence of the layered structure of these materials.
the potential barrier for pancake vortices in HTc layered superconductors depends on the transport current amplitude and the initial position and size of the pinning centers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new models of pinning potential barrier, which are based on a geometrical approach to capturing interactions of vortices in layered HTc high-temperature superconductors with nano-sized defects and on the analysis of the transport current flow in these materials, including the derivation and solution of basic mathematical equations.
the influence of the transport current on the potential barrier in the layered HTc superconductor.
the development of the model of the pining potential barrier in layered superconductors, which can be used to describe the current-voltage characteristics in HTc superconducting materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new model of pinning potential barrier is a promising theoretical tool for the understanding of the current–village characteristics and critical current behavior in HTc layered superconductors, and that it may be useful for the development of HTc superconducting devices.
the proposed model can describe the current-voltage characteristics and critical currents in HTc layered superconductors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed model of the potential barrier in multigrid layered superconductor is very useful for the understanding and interpretation of experimental results on critical current density and current–voltage curves.

the model of the pining potential barrier is very useful to describe the transport current flow in HTc layered superconductors, especially for the case of the high current densities and the low temperatures.

the model proposed in this work could explain the experimental data of critical currents in the HTc layered superconductors, and the results of our computer simulation of critical current in these materials are in good agreement with those of experimental results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical current density of HTc superconductor is not only a function of temperature and magnetic field but it is also a function of current intensity.
the pinning potential barriers in HTc superconducting materials are not constant, as it is usually assumed, but are dependent on the transport current amplitude.
the pinning potential in HTc superconducting materials can be described as a function of the transport current intensity and initial position of pancake vortex in a nano-sized defect.
